Choose with caution: if you cannot stand for long periods in a noisy and dusty environment and wear protective equipment, avoid repetitive watching and measuring, or cannot accept shift work and overtime, the actual work will not match expectations.

Where is the boundary between crushing, grinding, and polishing machine setters, operators, and tenders and the adjacent equipment repair, metal processing, and rolling positions?

This table compares crushing, grinding, and polishing machine setters, operators, and tenders one by one with the adjacent industrial machinery mechanics, maintenance workers machinery, rolling machine setters, operators, and tenders, metal and plastic cutting, punching, and press machine setters, operators, and tenders, and grinding, lapping, polishing, and buffing machine tool setters, operators, and tenders across seven items, namely core purpose, main object and basis, core process, main output, responsible party, collaboration and supervision, and conclusion boundaries: adjacent positions all work in equipment or metal processing settings, but the object, whether they carry equipment repair responsibility, and the processing method and process object do not shift just because positions are adjacent; when comparing, verify item by item against actual duties and the process involved.
Core purpose
Set up and run crushing, grinding, and polishing equipment per work orders and specifications, ensuring continuous material flow, products that meet specifications, and verifiable operation records.

Core purposes of adjacent positions: industrial machinery mechanics and maintenance workers machinery are responsible for repairing, maintaining, and troubleshooting equipment and machinery; rolling machine setters, operators, and tenders roll metal and plastic; cutting, punching, and press machine setters, operators, and tenders are responsible for punching and shearing forming; grinding, lapping, polishing, and buffing machine tool setters, operators, and tenders are responsible for machine tool grinding, lapping, polishing, and buffing.
Main object and basis

Crushing, grinding, and polishing equipment, materials and ingredients, and products, as well as operation and quality records; the basis is work orders and production specifications, equipment operating and safety procedures, and machine guarding and lockout/tagout requirements.

Objects and bases of adjacent positions: machinery and equipment and repair procedures (industrial machinery mechanics, maintenance workers machinery), metal and plastic stock and rolling processes (rolling machine setters, operators, and tenders), sheet metal and punching and shearing dies (cutting, punching, and press machine setters, operators, and tenders), and machine tools and grinding processes (grinding, lapping, polishing, and buffing machine tool setters, operators, and tenders).
Core process

Work order and setup, operation watching, weighing and inspection records, anomaly reporting, and maintenance are editorial task summaries; before clearing and maintenance enter a hazardous area, the specific energy isolation verification and restart conditions must be verified separately.

Processes of adjacent positions: diagnose and dismantle and repair equipment (industrial machinery mechanics, maintenance workers machinery), control shape per the rolling process (rolling machine setters, operators, and tenders), form by punching and shearing per the die (cutting, punching, and press machine setters, operators, and tenders), and process per the grinding process (grinding, lapping, polishing, and buffing machine tool setters, operators, and tenders).
Main output
Setup and operation records, weighing and measurement data, sampling and laboratory submission records, anomaly and repair report records, and product judgment records.

Outputs of adjacent positions: servicing and maintenance records (industrial machinery mechanics, maintenance workers machinery), rolled formed products (rolling machine setters, operators, and tenders), punched formed parts (cutting, punching, and press machine setters, operators, and tenders), and ground machined parts (grinding, lapping, polishing, and buffing machine tool setters, operators, and tenders).
Responsible party

Operators and watchers in this occupation are responsible for setting up and running per specifications, watching equipment status, and truthfully weighing, recording, and judging products; equipment repair authorization and process responsibility must follow employer procedures and are not decided unilaterally by them.
Responsible parties of adjacent positions: repair staff are responsible for equipment repair quality; metal processing positions are responsible for their own forming and processing quality.
Collaboration and supervision

For anomalies or blockages, first handle the danger per the real equipment procedure and seek help, record and hand over beyond-authority repairs to the responsible person; a machine stop is not energy isolation, and entering a hazardous area to clear blockages or perform maintenance requires verifying isolation, stored energy, verification, and restart procedures, and must not be done on a supervisor's consent alone.
Collaboration of adjacent positions: repair staff collaborate with production and engineering departments; metal processing positions collaborate with process and quality inspection staff.
Conclusion boundaries

Similar job titles do not mean the same duties: whether the object is operation and watching of crushing, grinding, and polishing equipment, equipment repair, metal rolling, punching and shearing forming, or machine tool grinding, and whether they carry repair authorization or process setup responsibility, determine the scope of duties and the assessment method, and cannot be swapped by name.

The preparation levels and authorization conditions of adjacent positions do not apply to this occupation and must be verified item by item against each occupation's official material and the rules of the institution concerned.
Key occupational judgments

Six recurring professional judgments: whether the setup and parameters match the work order specifications; whether the equipment operating status is watched continuously with anomalies found in time; whether materials and products are weighed, measured, and sampled for laboratory testing at intervals; whether products are judged per specifications and nonconforming items handled correctly; whether records are truthful, complete, and traceable; and whether, on equipment anomalies, blockages, or safety risks, the machine is stopped, reported, and protected per procedures.

The production specifications must be determined from the work order, and mill grinding fineness and machine parameters set correctly; a setup error may cause nonconforming product or equipment damage.
Equipment operation must be observed to ensure continuous, safe, and efficient flow and to detect faults, blockages, or wear in time; a lapse in watching may cause downtime and material loss.

Materials, ingredients, or products must be weighed and measured at intervals, inspected visually and by feel and with test equipment, and samples collected for laboratory testing; missed inspection may let nonconforming product flow into the next process.

Products must be judged conforming or not per established standards, nonconforming items removed, and the equipment readjusted to eliminate the problem; a wrong judgment may affect product quality and customer trust.
Judgment four: is the product judged per specifications and handled correctly?

Operation, test, and production data must be filled in promptly and truthfully on the designated forms, and silo identification must be clear; missing or false records will affect traceability and process improvement.
Judgment five: are records truthful, complete, and traceable?

Fictional situation: a crushing, grinding, and polishing machine setter, operator, or tender encounters four problems while on duty. details: China's 2021 safety regulations on dust explosion prevention in industrial and trade enterprises apply to designated industrial and trade enterprises with combustible dust explosion hazards, not to all mine sites or all inorganic dust positions. Articles 8 and 9 require the relevant personnel to pass special training and to have compliant PPE; Article 16 requires ignition source prevention in processes such as crushing and grinding; Article 19 requires that the relevant maintenance be restarted only after a specially approved plan, production stoppage, spark-free tools, and the working point temperature returning to normal, among other conditions; it cannot be done on a supervisor's consent alone or simply by pressing the stop button to clear a blockage and restart. Article 10 requires evacuation in fire and explosion response and prohibits measures that may raise dust, and specific equipment operation still follows the actual plan.

description.text: Crushing, grinding, and polishing machine setters, operators, and tenders (O*NET-SOC 51-9021.00) set up, operate, or tend crushing, grinding, and polishing machines: this covers setting the mill and grinding fineness per work orders and specifications, starting and adjusting machine controls, watching auxiliary equipment such as pumps and conveyors, weighing and measuring at intervals and sampling for laboratory testing, observing equipment operation to troubleshoot anomalies and blockages, cleaning, adjusting, and maintaining and reporting repairs, judging and removing nonconforming product, and recording operation and test data on forms; it includes the US 2025 median annual wage of 48,540 US dollars, about 28,700 people employed in 2024, a 2024—2034 employment projection decline (-1% or lower), about 2,700 ten-year openings including growth and replacement, industry employment concentrated in manufacturing (68%) and mining, quarrying, and oil and gas extraction (12%), the interest code RC, the Mainland China occupation-level wage gap, and the control points of machine guarding and lockout/tagout, dust, noise, and hand protection, and equipment status verification and record responsibility boundaries.

subject.summary: In the United States crushing, grinding, and polishing machine setters, operators, and tenders correspond to O*NET-SOC 51-9021.00 (Crushing, Grinding, and Polishing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders), who set up, operate, or tend machines used for crushing, grinding, or polishing materials, handling materials such as coal, glass, grain, stone, food, or rubber: setting the mill and grinding fineness per work orders and specifications, starting and adjusting machine controls, watching auxiliary equipment such as pumps and conveyors to keep material flowing, weighing or measuring materials and products at intervals and sampling for laboratory testing, observing equipment operation to find anomalies in time and clear blockages, cleaning, adjusting, and maintaining equipment and reporting needed repairs, judging and removing nonconforming product per specifications, and recording operation, test, and production data on the designated forms. The preparation level for this occupation is Job Zone 1-2 (usually requiring a high school diploma or equivalent and providing from a few days to one year of on-the-job training); the comparable positions on the Chinese side are crushing, grinding, and polishing equipment operation and watching positions in industries such as mineral processing, building materials, and food processing, whose duty and authorization bases do not correspond one-to-one with this US occupation segment and cannot be interchanged.
